reading.body:
Iron Mountain's 18 granted patents and 33 New Hampshire law exposure records show an information-management company patenting AI-adjacent techniques, but the data contains no direct evidence of compute, power, or grid capacity.

The patent titles cluster around automated data handling: self-labeling sample selection, predictive search, document image tokenization, and magnetic storage declassification. These are techniques for turning stored records into machine-readable inputs, which matters for AI because training pipelines depend on curated, labeled data at scale. But none of the patents mention compute hardware, power delivery, or facility construction.

The SEC filings show a standard public REIT reporting cadence, with quarterly and current reports through August 2026, and the New Hampshire law exposure count of 33 indicates legal or regulatory activity in its home state. This tells us Iron Mountain is an active corporate filer with some legal footprint, but it does not quantify energy demand, data center capacity, or grid interconnection. For understanding AI scaling constraints, this profile offers no direct evidence.

profile_text.body:
Iron Mountain is an enterprise information management company founded in 1951 and headquartered in Boston. It provides records management, secure information destruction and data backup and recovery to more than 220,000 customers in 58 countries.

Source: Wikipedia, Iron Mountain (company), retrieved 22 September 2026.
